47.0.0.en: 1 Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward: for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar. 2 Then brought he me out of the way of the gate northward, and led me about the way without unto the utter gate by the way that looketh eastward; and, behold, there ran out waters on the right side. 3 And when the man that had the line in his hand went forth eastward, he measured a thousand cubits, and he brought me through the waters; the waters were to the ankles. 4 Again he measured a thousand, and brought me through the waters; the waters were to the knees. Again he measured a thousand, and brought me through; the waters were to the loins. 5 Afterward he measured a thousand; and it was a river that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim in, a river that could not be passed over. 6 And he said unto me, "Son of man, hast thou seen this?" Then he brought me, and caused me to return to the brink of the river. 7 Now when I had returned, behold, at the bank of the river were very many trees on the one side and on the other. 8 Then said he unto me, "These waters issue out toward the east country, and go down into the desert, and go into the sea: which being brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed. 9 And it shall come to pass, that every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live: and there shall be a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither: for they shall be healed; and every thing shall live whither the river cometh. 10 And it shall come to pass, that the fishers shall stand upon it from Engedi even unto Eneglaim; they shall be a place to spread forth nets; their fish shall be according to their kinds, as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many. 11 But the miry places thereof and the marishes thereof shall not be healed; they shall be given to salt. 12 And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because its waters issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine."

47.0.1.en: In the mind of the Old Testament prophets, the age of the Messiah was the golden age for which the world had long waited, and they described it as an age rich in overflowing waters... We have already spoken of this matter, for the prophet Zechariah sees in these holy waters the mystery of the purification of the people (Zech 13:1), the prophet Joel the mystery of its sanctification (Joel 3:18), and the prophet Isaiah the mystery of the wilderness being turned into flowering fields (Isa 44:3, etc.)... As for the prophet Ezekiel, he sees the Lord having washed humanity and cleansed her of her uncleannesses, when He says to her, "Then washed I thee with water; yea, I throughly washed away thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee with oil" (Ezek 16:9). He also concludes his discourse on the new temple with his description of the holy waters coming down from under the threshold of the house eastward, from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar (Ezek 47:1-12). The following is to be noted in this discourse:

47.0.2.en: A. The prophet Ezekiel saw the waters coming out from under the threshold of the house eastward, "for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar" [1]. What is this house facing the east but the Church of the New Testament, which faces the Lord Christ as its east, and embraces the holy altar on which the sacrifice of the New Testament is offered? As for these holy waters that come out from under its threshold, they are holy Baptism, without which no one can enter into membership in the Church of Christ. These waters draw their power from the sacrifice, as the Apostle says: "There are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one" (1 Jn 5:8). This is Christian Baptism, which is the work of the Holy Spirit, who works in it through the blood of the Lord Christ.

47.0.3.en: These waters purify the world. As St. Jerome says: [When the world falls into sin, no one can purify it again except the fountain of waters].

47.1.0.en: B. The prophet Ezekiel saw a man who measured a thousand cubits and brought him through the waters, then a second thousand, and a third, and at the fourth he says: "It was a river that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim in, a river that could not be passed over. And he said unto me, Son of man, hast thou seen this? Then he brought me, and caused me to return to the brink of the river" [5-7]. What is this scene but the leading of the prophet Ezekiel into the mystery of Baptism?! We know that the number 1000 points to the heavenly life, for "one day is with the Lord as a thousand years," as though the prophet Ezekiel entered the heavenly life through Baptism. As for the thousand being repeated four times, it is because the work of Baptism embraces the peoples of the world, the Gentiles and peoples coming from every part of the world (the east, the west, the north and the south), that the believers may be dyed with a heavenly dye. Then the prophet contemplated the mysteries of Baptism and found that they surpass all human comprehension, for he saw them like a river that cannot be crossed, and he was obliged to return to the bank to contemplate God's work with people through these holy waters.

47.1.1.en: C. The prophet's question, "Son of man, hast thou seen this?", reminds us of God's saying to Adam, "Where art thou?" Since Adam had lost the splendor of his nature and his glories in Paradise, he now regains what he had lost. This is the secret of the question of wonder.

47.2.0.en: D. On his return to the bank, the prophet saw "very many trees on the one side and on the other" [7]. This is a symbolic picture of the believers planted by the streams of the holy waters, who give their fruit in its season, whose leaf does not wither, and in all that they do they prosper (Ps 1:3). These are the believers upon whom the Holy Spirit has descended, so that they became very many trees in the paradise of the Lord.

47.3.0.en: E. He also saw "a very great multitude of fish, because these waters shall come thither: for they shall be healed; and every thing shall live whither the river cometh" [9]. He saw the fish, and behold, they were of many kinds, "as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many" [10]. As the trees point to the believers who are likened to the Lord Christ, "the tree of life," so the fish point to the believers who are likened to the Lord Christ, "the Fish (Ichthys)," living in the waters of Baptism. As Origen says: [Christ is figuratively called the Fish]. And Tertullian says: [We, little fishes, after the example of our Fish, Jesus Christ, are born in water, and we are not safe in any other way than by remaining in the water continually].

47.4.0.en: G. He speaks of the sanctification of the waters, saying: "because its waters issued out of the sanctuary" [12].

47.5.0.en: 13 "Thus saith the Lord GOD; This shall be the border, whereby ye shall inherit the land according to the twelve tribes of Israel: Joseph shall have two portions. 14 And ye shall inherit it, one as well as another: concerning the which I lifted up mine hand to give it unto your fathers: and this land shall fall unto you for inheritance. 15 And this shall be the border of the land toward the north side, from the great sea, the way of Hethlon, as men go to Zedad; 16 Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazar-hatticon, which is by the coast of Hauran. 17 And the border from the sea shall be Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus, and the north northward, and the border of Hamath. And this is the north side. 18 And the east side ye shall measure from Hauran, and from Damascus, and from Gilead, and from the land of Israel by Jordan, from the border unto the east sea. And this is the east side. 19 And the south side southward, from Tamar even to the waters of strife in Kadesh, the river to the great sea. And this is the south side southward. 20 The west side also shall be the great sea from the border, till a man come over against Hamath. This is the west side. 21 So shall ye divide this land unto you according to the tribes of Israel. 22 And it shall come to pass, that ye shall divide it by lot for an inheritance unto you, and to the strangers that sojourn among you, which shall beget children among you: and they shall be unto you as born in the country among the children of Israel; they shall have inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel. 23 And it shall come to pass, that in what tribe the stranger sojourneth, there shall ye give him his inheritance, saith the Lord GOD."

47.5.1.en: After speaking of the holy temple and the holy city, he begins to define the holy land that He promised His people, and its division among the tribes, and here we note:

47.6.0.en: A. He says: "I lifted up mine hand to give it unto your fathers: and this land shall fall unto you for inheritance" [14]. It is as though He gives them assurance that He will not break the oath that He swore (by lifting up His hand) to their fathers; He remains faithful in spite of man's unfaithfulness.

47.6.1.en: B. The Lord Himself defined the position of the land with all its borders on every side, for God cares for His children and defines for them their dwelling for their comfort.

47.6.2.en: C. The Lord gave the tribe of Joseph two portions [13], so that the land might be divided into twelve parts, because the tribe of Levi has no portion in the land, but the Lord Himself is its portion. The division is to be by lot, so that no opportunity is given for personal factors to interfere in determining the portion of each tribe [22].

47.7.0.en: D. The strangers dwelling in their midst were given the right to share in the inheritance [22-23], pointing to the entry of the Gentiles into the eternal inheritance through the preaching of the Gospel, when all are one in Christ without distinction (Rom 10:12).

47.7.2.en: *Your prophet Zechariah saw in Your waters purification, Joel sanctification, and Isaiah fruitfulness, as my wasteland is turned into a garden for You.

47.7.3.en: And Ezekiel saw washing and cleansing from our uncleannesses, and the renewal of our nature!

47.7.5.en: It is washing, sanctification, fruitfulness and illumination; on its banks are holy trees, a divine garden.

47.7.6.en: Within it are fish in great abundance!

47.7.7.en: Grant me to live in the waters of Your Baptism, that I may live and grow continually!

47.7.8.en: *Do not deprive me of the portion that You have prepared for me in the new land.

47.7.9.en: Your Baptism brings me into the inheritance of Your glory, O You who are wonderful in Your greatness.

48.0.0.en: 1 "Now these are the names of the tribes. From the north end to the coast of the way of Hethlon, as one goeth to Hamath, Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus northward, to the coast of Hamath, a portion for Dan. And he shall have one portion from the east side unto the west side. 2 And by the border of Dan, from the east side unto the west side, a portion for Asher. 3 And by the border of Asher, from the east side even unto the west side, a portion for Naphtali. 4 And by the border of Naphtali, from the east side unto the west side, a portion for Manasseh. 5 And by the border of Manasseh, from the east side unto the west side, a portion for Ephraim. 6 And by the border of Ephraim, from the east side even unto the west side, a portion for Reuben. 7 And by the border of Reuben, from the east side unto the west side, a portion for Judah. 8 And by the border of Judah, from the east side unto the west side, shall be the offering which ye shall offer, five and twenty thousand in breadth, and in length as one of the other parts, from the east side unto the west side: and the sanctuary shall be in the midst of it. 9 The oblation that ye shall offer unto the LORD shall be five and twenty thousand in length, and ten thousand in breadth. 10 And for them, even for the priests, shall be this holy oblation; toward the north five and twenty thousand in length, and toward the west ten thousand in breadth, and toward the east ten thousand in breadth, and toward the south five and twenty thousand in length: and the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in the midst thereof. 11 It shall be for the priests that are sanctified of the sons of Zadok; which have kept my charge, which went not astray when the children of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray. 12 And this oblation of the land that is offered shall be unto them a thing most holy by the border of the Levites. 13 "And over against the border of the priests the Levites shall have five and twenty thousand in length, and ten thousand in breadth: all the length shall be five and twenty thousand, and the breadth ten thousand. 14 And they shall not sell of it, neither exchange, nor alienate the firstfruits of the land: for it is holy unto the LORD. 15 And the five thousand, that are left in the breadth over against the five and twenty thousand, shall be a profane place for the city, for dwelling, and for suburbs: and the city shall be in the midst thereof. 16 And these shall be the measures thereof; the north side four thousand and five hundred, and the south side four thousand and five hundred, and on the east side four thousand and five hundred, and the west side four thousand and five hundred. 17 And the suburbs of the city shall be toward the north two hundred and fifty, and toward the south two hundred and fifty, and toward the east two hundred and fifty, and toward the west two hundred and fifty. 18 And the residue in length over against the oblation of the holy portion shall be ten thousand eastward, and ten thousand westward: and it shall be over against the oblation of the holy portion; and the increase thereof shall be for food unto them that serve the city. 19 And as for them that serve the city, they shall serve it out of all the tribes of Israel. 20 All the oblation shall be five and twenty thousand by five and twenty thousand: foursquare ye shall offer the holy oblation, with the possession of the city. 21 And the residue shall be for the prince, on the one side and on the other of the holy oblation, and of the possession of the city, over against the five and twenty thousand of the oblation toward the east border, and westward over against the five and twenty thousand toward the west border, over against the portions for the prince: and the holy oblation and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst thereof. 22 Moreover from the possession of the Levites, and from the possession of the city, being in the midst of that which is the prince's, between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin, shall be for the prince. 23 And as for the rest of the tribes: from the east side unto the west side, Benjamin shall have one portion. 24 And by the border of Benjamin, from the east side unto the west side, Simeon shall have one portion. 25 And by the border of Simeon, from the east side unto the west side, Issachar one portion. 26 And by the border of Issachar, from the east side unto the west side, Zebulun one portion. 27 And by the border of Zebulun, from the east side unto the west side, Gad one portion. 28 And by the border of Gad, at the south side southward, the border shall be even from Tamar unto the waters of strife in Kadesh, and to the river toward the great sea. 29 This is the land which ye shall divide by lot unto the tribes of Israel for inheritance, and these are their portions, saith the Lord GOD."

48.0.1.en: In brief, the vision defined the division of the holy land as follows:

48.0.2.en: A. It assigned seven tribes north of the temple [1-7] and five tribes south of the temple [23-29], so that the temple thus represents the beating heart of all the portions, the secret of the life of their inhabitants and of their sanctification.

48.0.3.en: B. Before the captivity the people were divided into two kingdoms, one comprising ten tribes whom Assyria took captive, and the other comprising two tribes whom Babylon took captive... But here, under the rich grace of God, in the new temple, there is the one kingdom of Christ, without division.

48.1.0.en: C. The defining of the land of the temple and the priests (8-11): where the temple is, there are the priests who serve it, and to them the offerings are presented. Once again he affirms the reward of the sons of Zadok for their faithfulness to the sanctity of the temple when the Levites went astray [11]; therefore they alone, and none besides them, deserved to offer the sacrifices on the altar and to draw near to these holy things.

48.1.1.en: D. The division here is entirely different from the division that took place in the days of Joshua the son of Nun, and the interpreters hold that this division cannot be understood literally but is to be understood in a symbolic sense.

48.1.2.en: In the division of the land of Canaan in the days of Joshua the son of Nun, the tribe of Dan received its portion at the end of all the tribes (Josh 19:40), whereas here it receives its portion at the beginning of all the tribes [2]. It is as though the divine revelation wishes to assure us that on the day of the Lord we shall see wonderful things that we did not expect... Those who were first become last, and those who were last become first.

48.1.3.en: Origen says: [We find here great giants who appear as little children on the day of the Lord, and the reverse also. He also says that we see men who were heroes in outward faith appear weak, and also the reverse!].

48.1.4.en: It is as though the day of the Lord reveals wonderful hidden things that we do not expect!

48.1.5.en: E. Each tribe takes its portion from God as suits it, receiving what suffices it so that it is in no want, to say with the Psalmist: "He shall choose our inheritance for us, the excellency of Jacob whom he loved" (Ps 47:4). It is to be noted that the border of each tribe forms a border for the other tribe, a sign of fellowship and unity through shared holy love.

48.2.0.en: F. The land set apart for service may not be disposed of by sale or exchange, nor are firstfruits offered from it, because it itself represents a firstfruit to the Lord, holy to Him [14].

48.2.1.en: G. The holy city is square in shape, its sides equal on every side, as the cities of the Levites were formerly... and it, as some interpreters see, cannot be applied in practice in a literal way, but it represents the city of the living God.

48.3.0.en: Its inhabitants were formerly mostly from Judah and also Benjamin, since the city lay on the border of the two tribes, but in the new city all the tribes work in it [19], as it represents the Kingdom of God on earth for all humanity.

48.3.1.en: H. The king is given a special portion suited to his responsibilities [1], that he may not covet the portions of the people.

48.4.0.en: 30 "And these are the goings out of the city on the north side, four thousand and five hundred measures. 31 And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates northward; one gate of Reuben, one gate of Judah, one gate of Levi. 32 And at the east side four thousand and five hundred: and three gates; and one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, one gate of Dan. 33 And at the south side four thousand and five hundred measures: and three gates; one gate of Simeon, one gate of Issachar, one gate of Zebulun. 34 At the west side four thousand and five hundred, with their three gates; one gate of Gad, one gate of Asher, one gate of Naphtali. 35 It was round about eighteen thousand: and the name of the city from that day shall be, Jehovah-shammah."

48.4.1.en: It is noted that it resembles the new city that St. John the Beloved saw, of which we have already spoken in our commentary on the Book of Revelation (chapter 21), in that it is square and has twelve gates, three gates on each side, signifying entry into heaven through the Holy Trinity, and a sign that its gates open toward the east, the west, the north and the south, to embrace believers from every tongue and nation. On the gates were inscribed the names of the tribes, a symbol of the universal Church, which embraces all the tribes of humanity.

48.4.2.en: It is also noted that he did not call the city "Jerusalem" nor "Canaan," but gave it a new name, "Jehovah-shammah," that is, "God is there." So St. John the Beloved heard a voice from heaven concerning this city, saying: "Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God" (Rev 21:3). It is as though the conclusion of the whole book is entering with God into a perpetual dwelling, and a fellowship and union in which we are found with Him and in Him, while He dwells in us forever.

48.4.3.en: The book began with a heavenly vision, in which was the awesome fiery divine chariot, and Ezekiel himself fell to the earth; from there came the divine judgment of chastising the people, and the departure of the glory of the Lord from the temple and the city; and the book ends with the opening of the gates of heaven before humanity from the east and the west, from all the nations, peoples and tongues, who enjoy the fellowship of the divine glory!

48.4.4.en: You are my portion! You are my glory!

48.4.5.en: * You opened the gates of heaven before Your prophet Ezekiel, and he was terrified before the fiery divine chariot and fell!

48.4.6.en: You raised him up and sustained him to proclaim Your mysteries!

48.4.7.en: He heard of the chastisements of the people and was troubled!

48.4.8.en: He saw Your glory departing from Your temple and Your city, and he grieved!

48.4.9.en: Behold, now You show him the plan of Your salvation: an open heaven, and a people of every tongue enjoying the fellowship of Your glory forever!

48.4.10.en: * Carry me to Your heavens; I want to see the Jerusalem above, to meet You face to face, and to cast myself into Your embrace forever!

48.4.12.en: You are my joy and the gladness of my heart!

48.4.13.en: You are my crown and my glory!

48.4.14.en: When shall I see You and remain with You, O desire of my heart?!
